歹 (skeletal remains) — the corpse being mourned, the source of 死's meaning 'to die, dead.'
亻 (person) — 傻 describes a state of mind a person is in.
囟 (the top of the head), together with a striking motion below, pictures someone being hit on the head — the odd image behind 傻's meaning 'foolish.'
Represents the round shape of a melon hanging on the vine.

components.note: 艹 (plant) — 英 originally meant 'flower, blossom,' later borrowed for 'outstanding, hero' and to write 'England, English.'
央 (yāng) gives a sound hint — 英 is pronounced yīng, sharing the initial consonant and a nasal final, though the vowel has shifted.
田 (farmland) over 土 (earth/soil) — originally referred to a village or a measured unit of farmland, later extended to mean 'inside' or a unit of distance.
扌 (hand) — 挑 describes an action done with the hand, picking or carrying.
兆 (zhào) gives a sound distantly related to tiāo, having drifted apart over time.
戈 (a dagger-axe, a weapon) — 战 relates to fighting and war.
占 (zhàn) gives the sound — 战 is also pronounced zhàn, an exact match.
匕 (a kneeling person) — a mourner bowed down in grief.
歹 (skeletal remains) — the corpse being mourned, the source of 死's meaning 'to die, dead.'
A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.
耳 (ear) — an old link between listening to official duties and 职's meaning 'duty, profession, office'
只 (zhī) gives a loose sound connection to 职's reading zhí
土 (earth/soil) — 地's original meaning is 'earth, ground'
也 (yě) gives a partial sound match for 地's other reading dì; in this grammatical-particle usage the character is instead pronounced 'de'
Earth — a site is a piece of land.
Gives the sound zhǐ, matching the character's reading.
The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'
少 depicts a few small dots or grains, like scattered sand — a simple picture of a small quantity, giving the meaning 'few' or 'little.'
土 (earth/soil) — 地's original meaning is 'earth, ground'
也 (yě) gives a partial sound match for 地's other reading dì; in this grammatical-particle usage the character is instead pronounced 'de'
犭 (dog) on the left represents a guard dog.
讠 (speech) suggests an accusation or a legal case being spoken.
犬 (dog) on the right completes the scene, giving 狱 its meaning 'prison, lawsuit.'
Traditionally analyzed as 日 combined with 疋, linked to the idea of speaking directly and truthfully — the source of 是's meaning 'to be, indeed, right.'
A picture of a nose; because people in ancient China would point to their own nose when referring to themselves, the character came to mean 'self.'
Originally depicted a hand 扌 gripping a weapon 戈; this original meaning was later borrowed to represent the pronoun 'I/we.'

亻 (a person) — someone receiving something

Daoist or Buddhist ceremony for the souls of the dead

components.note: 女 (woman) — represents a mother.
子 (child/son) — a mother together with her child was seen as an image of goodness, giving 好 its meaning 'good.'
礻 (spirit, ritual) — 祈 concerns communicating with the spirits or gods.
斤 (jīn) gives a sound distantly related to qí, having drifted apart over time.
礻 (spirit) — 祷 concerns communicating with the spirits or gods.
寿 (shòu) gives a sound distantly related to dǎo, having drifted apart over time.
攵 (a hand with an implement) — relates to 收's meaning 'to receive, collect, harvest.'
丩 (jiū) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from shōu.
扌 (hand) — picking something up is done with the hand.
合 (to gather, combine) contributes to the character's form, describing the action of gathering things up.
宀 (roof) — represents a home.
各 (each, various) — a person arriving from elsewhere and welcomed under one's roof gave 客 its meaning 'guest, visitor.'
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.
犬 (dog) — an old, now-opaque link behind 状's meaning 'form, shape, condition'
丬 (qiáng) gives a loose sound connection to 状's reading zhuàng
心 (heart/mind) — 态 relates to one's inner state, manner, or attitude
太 (tài) gives the sound — 态 is also pronounced tài, an exact match
冂 depicts a boundary or border enclosing an area.
土 (earth/land) — the land enclosed within the border.
口 here depicts a well within that land — together giving 周 its early meaning of a bounded territory, and later 'circumference, week, the Zhou dynasty.'
囗 (an enclosure) — 围 relates to surrounding or encircling something
韦 (wéi) gives the sound — 围 is also pronounced wéi, an exact match
扌 (hand) — 报 relates to taking action against someone.
卩 (a kneeling or bound person) — handling a wrongdoer and announcing the judgment gave 报 its meaning 'to report' or 'to announce.'
辶 (to walk) — 道 relates to a path or road one walks along.
首 (shǒu) is the historical phonetic element; its modern reading no longer resembles dào, a reminder that sound components can drift after thousands of years of pronunciation change.
彡 (shān) is the historical phonetic component of 参; sound change over time has left little resemblance to the modern reading cān
辶 (walking/movement) — relates to 运's meaning 'to move, transport,' and by extension 'fortune,' the movement of one's life.
云 (yún) gives a sound hint — 运 is pronounced yùn, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
力 (strength/force) — 动 relates to movement produced by exertion or force.
彳 (to walk, step) — 彼 originally related to distance, extended to mean 'that, the other.'
皮 (pí) gives a sound close to bǐ.
匕 here relates to a person crouching or sitting — 此 originally pictured 'this place' where someone is.
止 (zhǐ) gives a hint of the sound — 此 is pronounced cǐ, sharing a similar final though the initial has shifted over time.
艹 (grass) forms the top of the character.
木 (tree), sheltered beneath a covering, together depict plants flourishing, giving 荣 its meaning 'glory, prosperity.'
The upper part, related to 土, traditionally depicted one person's fate.
干 depicted a contrasting fate — the character set two outcomes side by side, with the fortunate one giving 幸 its meaning 'lucky, fortunate.'
人 (people) over 云 (clouds/say) — a picture of people gathering and speaking together, related to 会's meanings 'to meet' and 'to know how to.'
讠 (speech) — relates to 议's meaning 'to discuss, deliberate; opinion.'
义 (yì) gives the sound — 议 is also pronounced yì, an exact match.
至 (zhì, to arrive) — carries 到's core meaning, 'to reach, to arrive'
刂 (a form of 刀, dāo) gives a sound close to 到's pronunciation dào
辶 (walking/movement) — relates to 达's meaning 'to reach, arrive, achieve.'
大 (dà) gives the sound — 达 is pronounced dá, a close match sharing the same rhyme.
日 (sun) — 显 relates to something bright and clearly visible in the light
业 (yè) gives a loose sound connection to 显's reading xiǎn
A pictograph of an altar or offering table used in ancestor worship — presenting offerings extended to 示's meaning 'to show, display, indicate.'
阝 (a mound or place) — 队 pictures people gathering together.
人 (person) — people gathering in one place gave 队 its meaning 'a team' or 'a line/queue.'
亻 (person) — 伍 counts out a group of people.
五 (five) — five 五 people 亻 standing together gave 伍 its meaning 'a squad of five, a group.'
立 depicts a person standing with arms and legs spread, on a horizontal line representing the ground — a simple picture of standing upright.
刂 (a knife) — 刻 relates to carving with a blade
亥 (hài) is the historical phonetic element; it no longer closely matches 刻's modern reading kè
纟 (thread) — 绝 originally meant to sever a thread completely, extended to mean 'to cut off, absolute'
色 (sè) gives a loose sound connection to 绝's reading jué
The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'
無-shaped top pictures a dancer holding decorated sleeves or fans.
舛 below pictures a pair of feet, together giving 舞 its meaning 'to dance.'
女 (woman) — 奶 relates to a woman nursing, and to milk.
乃 (nǎi) is an exact match for the sound of 奶.
女 (woman) — 奶 relates to a woman nursing, and to milk.
乃 (nǎi) is an exact match for the sound of 奶.
又 (a hand) — reaching to take hold of something.
耳 (ear) — from an ancient battlefield practice of taking a fallen enemy's ear as proof of a kill, the origin of 取's meaning 'to take, obtain.'
氵 (water) — relates to 消's meaning 'to disappear, dissolve,' like something dissolving in water.
肖 (xiào) gives a sound hint — 消 is pronounced xiāo, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
亠 — read as the head of an animal standing upright in this pictograph; the character was later reused for the unrelated meaning 'to leave, be apart from, distance.'
女 (woman) — 婚 relates to marriage, historically centered on the wife.
昏 (hūn) gives the sound — an exact match with 婚.
⺮ (bamboo) — 等 pictures bamboo strips, once used as writing tablets, being sorted.
寺 (originally a government office, later 'temple') — sorting and arranging bamboo documents at an official court gave 等 its meanings 'to wait,' 'rank,' and 'etc.'
彳 (a road/step) — someone arriving on the road
寺 (a court/hall) — the destination where the visitor is welcomed
冖 (a roof/house) — the home being welcomed into.
友 (a friend) — brought close into one's home; the traditional form 愛 also includes 心 ('heart') in the middle — the source of 爱's meaning 'to love.'
忄 (heart) — 情 relates to feelings and emotions.
青 (qīng) gives the sound — 情 is pronounced qíng, a close match differing only in tone.
力 depicts the blade of a plow — since plowing fields took great physical effort, the shape came to represent strength or power.
八 (to divide/split apart) — represents something already split into parts.
刀 (knife) — a knife cutting already-divided pieces further, giving 分 its meaning 'to divide, to separate.'
酋 pictures a jar of wine.
寸 (hand) below offers it up respectfully, giving 尊 its meaning 'to respect, to honor.'
千 (thousand) — 重 pictures a heavy burden carried a great distance.
里 (a unit of distance, like a mile) — carrying something a thousand 里 emphasizes how heavy and significant a burden it is, giving 重 its meaning 'heavy' or 'important.'
攵 (a hand with a stick) — 教 relates to instructing or disciplining, the traditional action of teaching.
孝 (xiào) gives a hint of the sound — 教 is pronounced jiào, a connection that has shifted somewhat.
扌 (hand) — 授 means to give or hand something over.
受 (shòu) gives the sound — an exact match with 授.
干 (originally a person) shown carrying a heavy load of grain on their back — since harvests came once a year, the character came to mean 'year.'
走 (to walk/run) — 超 relates to overtaking or surpassing someone while moving
召 (zhào) gives a sound distantly related to 超's reading chāo, having drifted apart over time
辶 (to walk/move) — shows 过's core meaning of 'passing through' or 'crossing'
咼 (guō) gives a sound close to 过's reading guò; the simplified form 过 now uses 寸 in place of 咼, but the phonetic connection traces back to the traditional character 過
廾 (two hands) — depicts hands at work.
一 represents the latch or bar of a door; hands lifting it away gave 开 its meaning 'to open, to start.'
A simplified form of 車, a pictograph of a two-wheeled cart seen from above — the wheels, axle, and frame are visible in the original shape — the source of 车's meaning 'cart, vehicle.'

meanings: the arches, loops and whorls on the fingers

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 指 relates to using the hand, specifically the fingers.
旨 (an aim, purpose) — combined with 扌 (hand), 指 came to mean 'finger' and 'to point,' aiming the hand at something.
Thread/silk — patterns were originally woven into cloth.
Gives the sound wén, matching the character's reading.
广 (a building/shelter) — the setting of the celebration.
大 (great, big) — a grand event held inside, together giving 庆 its meaning 'to celebrate.'
礻 (altar, spirit) on the left sets a religious scene.
兄 (a person, shown here kneeling or speaking) on the right shows someone praying, giving 祝 its meaning 'to wish, to pray for blessings.'
亻 (person) — the one settling somewhere.
主 (host, master) — the idea of a person settled in a place as if hosting it, giving 住 its meaning 'to live, reside, stay.'
手 is a simple picture of an open hand with the fingers spread out.
亻 (person) — 偶 originally described a wooden figure or idol shaped like a person, later extending to 'a pair' and 'by chance.'
禺 (yú) gives a sound distantly related to 偶's reading ǒu, having drifted apart over time.
亻 (person) — relates to 像's meaning 'to resemble, be like; image, portrait,' comparing one person or thing to another.
象 (xiàng) gives the sound — 像 is also pronounced xiàng, an exact match.
凡 (common/ordinary) — suggests something shared or held in common.
口 (mouth) — sharing a common mouth/voice with others gave 同 its meaning of 'same, together.'
士 (a scholar/gentleman) — represents a person of learning and ambition.
心 (heart/mind) — the mind and aspirations of a scholar gave 志 its meaning 'purpose, will, ambition.'
衤 (clothes) — 裤 names a piece of clothing, trousers.
库 (kù) gives the sound — an exact match with 裤.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.
冖 here is a distorted form of 力 (strength) — a simplified way of showing soldiers grouped together.
车 (cart/vehicle) — 军 originally pictured soldiers riding out to battle in war chariots.
阝 (a mound or place) — 队 pictures people gathering together.
人 (person) — people gathering in one place gave 队 its meaning 'a team' or 'a line/queue.'
